page: UpCloud GPU-48xCPU-480GB-2xB200 is a GPU-accelerated server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8570 processor with 48 physical cores and 48 vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 480.0 GB of system memory, providing 10.0 GB per core. For acceleration, it integrates two NVIDIA Blackwell B200 GPUs with a combined VRAM of 384 GB. No local storage is bundled with this instance type.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core processing and memory performance. The server achieved a PassMark CPU score of 88533.65 and a stress-ng multi-core CPU performance score of 97240.84, both placing in the top tier and strong categories respectively. Large block memory read bandwidth reached a top-tier speed of 385.14 GB/sec, while write bandwidth was measured at 134.73 GB/sec. For specialized workloads, the system demonstrated high efficiency in LLM inference, processing 9458.91 tokens per second for prompt processing on a small 135M model, alongside a top-tier database operations score of 33288.64.

The server's hardware profile offers high resource density for parallel computing and machine learning tasks, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for GPU-heavy workloads. However, certain architectural tradeoffs exist. The CPU allocation is shared rather than dedicated, which may introduce performance variability under sustained CPU-bound loads. Additionally, the complete lack of local storage requires users to configure external storage solutions, which could impact overall I/O latency.

This configuration is designed for workloads requiring massive parallel processing and high-capacity GPU memory. Suitable use cases include large language model inference, deep learning training, high-performance database operations, and complex physics simulations.
